study: Rudd et al. 2017, MathsFlip Flipped Learning (EEF)
eval_evidence: EEF efficacy trial independently evaluated by NFER / Institute for Effective Education; the program was developed by Shireland Collegiate Academy, a separate party.
developer_evidence: Shireland Collegiate Academy staff (directors, project manager, e-learning team) — the program's developers — trained the Year 5 teachers over two days and provided ongoing support (report 'Staff from Shireland trained Year 5 teachers').
cascade_evidence: Shireland (developer) staff trained the participating primary-school teachers directly; no train-the-trainer hop.
counterfactual_evidence: 12 control schools delivered maths lessons 'in the usual' way; true BAU control.
coaching_evidence: Project manager made regular visits, provided feedback on lessons and 'coached teachers who needed extra support', plus periodic in-school workshops; periodic support rather than recurring monthly in-class coaching cycles.
student_dose_evidence: Flipped-learning reorganizes the teacher's regular maths instruction (pupils preview content via the MathsFlip platform); no separate tutoring/pull-out or extra instructional minutes added beyond regular class teaching.
maturity_evidence: Trial teachers were trained over 2 days and delivered MathsFlip Apr 2014-Apr 2015; outcomes (KS2 2015) measured in these schools' first implementation year (teachers new to it).
